summary: A single-author measurement study of AI-system delivery records. A documentation survey grades 47 platforms (20 CI/CD, 27 model-serving/agent) on four record dimensions under a three-label protocol, in two Claude-produced grading passes (the second blind) adjudicated by the author. It finds no platform documenting default emission of a content-addressed identity over the 'behavioral tuple' (model version, instructions, tool definitions, retrieval and runtime config), while 16 of 27 agent platforms default to nominal immutable versions. A read-only instrument over 30 public GitHub repos finds that 7 of 15 attestation adopters publish source-only releases, so their declared binding cannot be checked, and that 5 of 7 measurable adopters realize it end to end. No pipeline in which an agent operates the loop is measured.

claims.claim: No surveyed platform's default record emits a content-addressed behavioral-tuple identity (0 of 47)
claims.evidence: §6, §7.2: a bounded negative existence claim over documentation, every cell with pinned pages. Raw agreement between passes 78/108 on the agent class, no chance-corrected statistic. Both passes were Claude sessions.

claims.claim: Immutable nominal versioning is arriving as the agent platforms' default (16 of 27)
claims.evidence: §6.2, §7.2. Nominal-split agreement 21/27. The author concedes affirmative counts are upper bounds because documentation is graded generously.

claims.claim: Seven of 15 attestation adopters publish source-only releases (binding unverifiable); five of seven measurable adopters realize the binding end to end
claims.evidence: §4.1, §7.1: 30 repositories, 1,116 archived API responses. Grading agreement 23/30 (intended depth) and 19/30 (realized depth). A post-reconciliation correction moved 9 cells to undetermined.

claims.claim: Records in agentic software engineering are structurally short of justifiability
claims.evidence: §8 concedes that no pipeline in which an agent operates the loop is measured: agent-class evidence is documentation only, and the corollary linking survey to gap is 'definitional, conceded as such' (§7.2).

patterns.note: Proposes content-addressed audit records of the agent's behavioral configuration (model version, instructions, tool definitions, retrieval/runtime config) at promotion, with a check that can refuse. It only measures that platforms do not emit this by default; no effect on outcomes is measured.
Traceability here means binding the evaluated artifact to the deployed artifact, not requirement-to-code. It argues that traceability records should support a refusing check.
Approval records with actor and time are default on 13/20 CI/CD and 8/27 agent platforms per documentation; gates themselves are not evaluated.

methodology.sample: 47 platforms x 4 dimensions (188 cells) graded from pinned documentation; 30 public GitHub Actions repositories in two strata of 15
methodology.models: Anthropic Claude / Claude Code performed both grading passes and the analysis tooling (AI usage disclosure)
methodology.variance: Raw inter-pass agreement only (17/20, 55/60, 78/108; 23/30, 19/30); no chance-corrected statistics

standards.artifacts: Survey record, pin log, frozen frame, collector, hashed archive, grading passes and analyzer at github.com/mentu-ai/from-traceability-to-justifiability (public)
standards.preregistration: An OSF registration (10.17605/OSF.IO/D3JFV) covers a separate confirmatory study deliberately not reported; this paper's analyses are descriptive

biases.detail: Both 'independent' grading passes were Claude sessions, adjudicated by the sole author, with no human-vs-LLM agreement check. The abstract's 'graded twice (second pass blind)' does not say the graders were LLMs.
The title and abstract frame agentic software engineering, but the body measures platform documentation and artifact-layer CI/CD attestation; §8 concedes the agentic setting is unmeasured.
30 repositories; 7 measurable adopters carry the realization result.
The 'justifiability' ladder reframes the known nominal-vs-content-addressed identity problem from software supply chains (the author acknowledges the lineage).
A single author defines the protocol, runs the LLM graders and reconciles divergences.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: none directly; the motivating case is a client estate with a bespoke binding artifact
coi.detail: The author's venture may benefit from the argument that platforms lack content-addressed behavioral identity, but no product is evaluated.

verdict_reason: Off-topic for this KB: release-provenance records for AI systems and CI/CD attestation, not software development with LLM agents or its human side. Its own threats section concedes no agent-operated pipeline is measured, and the gradings are LLM-produced and unvalidated. The archive is careful and public, but it does not inform the discovery or onboarding question.
applicability: Little for discovery and onboarding. One idea transfers to the harness's audit trail: when an agent-produced change merges, record a content hash of the configuration that produced it (model id, instruction files, skills, MCP tool schemas, retrieval/index version), not a mutable version name. Later reviewers and newcomers can then tell exactly which instructions and knowledge the agent had. The paper does not evaluate this.
